paragraphs.source_en: On the third day of the sixth month, while Tokugawa Ieyasu was struggling through the steep mountains along the road from Ōmi to Iga, Hashiba Chikuzen-no-kami Hideyoshi was inspecting the siege lines around Bitchū Takamatsu Castle with Hachisuka Hikoemon and Kuroda Kanbei. The downpour that had continued since morning had finally stopped, but the ground remained wet and slippery. The horses stumbled now and then, making attendants such as Ishida Sakichi and Ichiyanagi Ichisuke, who followed behind, secretly chuckle.

units.source_zh: “官兵卫对安国寺可说了如指掌，那么，叫惠琼的那和尚，确实得到了小早川和吉川的信赖，并给他们出谋划策了吗？”

paragraphs.source_zh: “官兵卫对安国寺可说了如指掌，那么，叫惠琼的那和尚，确实得到了小早川和吉川的信赖，并给他们出谋划策了吗？”

paragraphs.source_en: “Yes. My lord may trust Kanbei on that.”

units.source_en: “Yes. My lord may trust Kanbei on that.”

paragraphs.source_en: “Then he truly is a remarkable man. I had thought him no more than an abbot.”

units.source_en: “Then he truly is a remarkable man. I had thought him no more than an abbot.”

paragraphs.source_en: Kanbei smiled wryly. “When Mōri Motonari was still alive, he visited Ekei in Aki and already perceived that Ekei was no ordinary young monk. Now he has become the extraordinary man you saw today, and he has praised you on more than one occasion.”

units.source_zh: 官兵卫苦笑了一下。

paragraphs.source_en: “What, praised me...? We must not lower our guard around that monk. A man who praises others so freely can never have good intentions.”

units.source_en: “What, praised me...? We must not lower our guard around that monk. A man who praises others so freely can never have good intentions.”

paragraphs.source_en: Mitsuhide had killed Nobunaga and his son? Hideyoshi instantly felt a chill run down his back, as though a keen blade had already been laid against his neck. But when he reconsidered, the whole thing seemed absurd.

paragraphs.source_en: Whatever else might be true, the captured messenger had behaved far too casually—the false blind man had deliberately approached the enemy camp and wandered slowly about. Had he been hurrying, people would instead have suspected him of being a secret messenger. He must have intended to be captured so that Hideyoshi would be shaken and hasten to make peace with the Mōri. After all, the five thousand soldiers in the castle were on the verge of starving to death.

paragraphs.source_en: “Exactly. After winning a battle, men often grow careless. I am no exception. I will not release a secret messenger for amusement, only to regret it afterward. That man had already lost the desire to live. Go and give the order to kill him.”
